reason: The contract explicitly requires correct group assignment "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size", with the trailing short group being its own group and scales/zeros supplied with ceil(K/group_size) rows. The host wrapper (kernel.py lines 69-73) instead computes num_groups = K // group_size (floor) and clamps the per-column table to num_groups-1, so the trailing short group can never index its own scale/zero row.\n\nProbe t6 (run_claim_probe on c1) built packed INT4 weights with the kernel's own zero+1 convention and supplied ceil(K/group_size) group rows. With K=48, group_size=32, bits=4, M=N=32 the kernel output differed from the contract-correct reference by max_abs_err=10.498 against ref_absmax=11.931 (rel 0.880), while matching a deliberately wrong "clamped" reference (columns 32..47 forced onto group row 0) to max_abs_err=2.86e-06 — i.e. bit-level agreement with the incorrect grouping, not a precision artifact. The K=64 control (exact multiple) matched the correct reference to 5.72e-06 (rel 2.7e-07), isolating the failure to the short final group exactly as the source predicted. Evidence finalized as c1.e1 (event t6), claim status confirmed, scope in_scope on problem.txt's explicit non-multiple-K requirement.
